The Albums page Open Albums from the sidebar to see everything in one place: a shelf for each collection, then your albums that aren't in a collection, then your shared spaces. Filter by All, My albums, Shared or Smart, and switch between grid and list. Sort albums by title, date created, last modified, newest or oldest photos, item count, or your own Custom order. In Custom order, drag an album onto another to put it just before. The New menu creates an album, a smart album, a collection or a shared space. Drag an album onto a collection to file it there, or out again to take it out. Press Escape to cancel a drag. Collections A collection is a shelf of albums, such as "2026" or "Trips". Albums sit inside a collection one level deep, and collections don't hold other collections. Deleting a collection keeps its albums in your library, on their own. Albums To add photos, select them in your library and choose Add to album, or open an album and add from there. In an album you can: edit the title and description in place see members and their roles, shared links, the album's map and a slideshow download the album, or pick an icon from thousands of symbols choose its cover, or let the cover follow the newest item with Always use the newest item arrange the photos in your own order, with the mouse or the keyboard like and comment in the activity panel, when the album is shared. The owner can turn this off under Options, then Likes and comments Set your Default album viewing order, newest or oldest first, in your preferences. An album someone has arranged by hand keeps its own order. Deleting an album never deletes its photos: they stay in your library, and only the album's sharing and public links are removed. A Locked photo is never used as a cover. Nested albums Drag albums into parent albums to build a tree, and use the breadcrumbs to move back up through it. Collections stay simple one-level shelves, so you can use both. Take a quick look inside a parent album before you delete it. Share an album Share an album with people on your server as an Editor, who can add their own photos, or a Viewer, who can only look. See Sharing. Smart albums A smart album fills itself from a rule, and keeps updating as new photos match. To make one, run a search and save it as a smart album, or choose New, then Smart album, and build the rule with a preview. Albums with a rule carry a small mark. A rule gathers only photos you can already see, so sharing stays exactly as you set it. For the ready-made albums such as Travel, Food and Pets, see Built-in smart albums. Everyone sees the whole story in one place, and everyone who adds a photo stays its owner. Roles Removing photos or members, or deleting the space, never deletes anyone's originals. Inside a space Each space has its own Photos, Albums, People, Map, Activity and Members views. When other members have added photos since you were last there, Show only what is new shows just those. Link album to add an album of your own. Its current and future photos appear in the space. Add photos in bulk. You see how many will be added first, and the work carries on in the background, even if the server restarts. A preview can include up to 100,000 photos. People names are private. articles.title: Casting to a TV
articles.description: Watch photos and videos with Google Cast from the web or Android, or play from iPhone on Apple TV.
articles.intro: Share your photos and videos on the big screen. The Frameleaf web app casts to Google Cast devices, such as a Chromecast or a Nest Hub, and the Android app has Google Cast built in. On iPhone, you can play straight to the Apple TV app.

headings.title: Web casting: why it's off by default
headings.text: To cast, the web app has to load Google's Cast scripts from Google's servers every time the page opens. Some people would rather their photo app didn't contact Google at all, so you choose whether to turn it on.

headings.title: Turn it on
headings.text: Open Settings from the sidebar and go to Your preferences, then Tools & sidebar. In the Cast to a TV row, turn on Use. Save your preferences.

headings.title: Cast a photo or video
headings.text: Open a photo or video in the viewer, choose the cast button, then pick your device. The cast button appears as soon as Frameleaf finds a compatible device.

headings.title: What your server needs
headings.text: Google Cast needs a few things from your server:

headings.title: From Android
headings.text: In the Android app, open a photo or video, choose the cast button and select a device on your network. Casting uses Google Play services. The button appears when the app finds a compatible receiver, or while you're already casting. Choose it again to stop.

headings.title: From iPhone to Apple TV
headings.text: Open Frameleaf on your iPhone and on the Frameleaf TV app, on the same network and signed in to the same Frameleaf account. On a collection page, choose Play on Apple TV, then pick the TV.

articles.text: Share your photos and videos on the big screen. The Frameleaf web app casts to Google Cast devices, such as a Chromecast or a Nest Hub, and the Android app has Google Cast built in. On iPhone, you can play straight to the Apple TV app. Web casting is experimental and off by default, so you turn it on when you want it. Web casting: why it's off by default To cast, the web app has to load Google's Cast scripts from Google's servers every time the page opens. Some people would rather their photo app didn't contact Google at all, so you choose whether to turn it on. Turn it on Open Settings from the sidebar and go to Your preferences, then Tools & sidebar. In the Cast to a TV row, turn on Use. Save your preferences. The setting is per account. If your administrator has turned casting off for your account, it says Turned off by your administrator. Cast a photo or video Open a photo or video in the viewer, choose the cast button, then pick your device. The cast button appears as soon as Frameleaf finds a compatible device. What your server needs Google Cast needs a few things from your server: HTTPS. Open Frameleaf over an HTTPS address to see the cast menu. A public HTTPS address. Your server must be reachable over HTTPS from the internet, and its DNS name must resolve through Google's public DNS servers (8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4). Compatible videos. Videos must be in a format Google Cast devices can play. From Android In the Android app, open a photo or video, choose the cast button and select a device on your network. Casting uses Google Play services. The button appears when the app finds a compatible receiver, or while you're already casting. Choose it again to stop. The TV loads your photo or video straight from its media address, so it needs to reach your server and play the video's format. If an item can't be cast, because it isn't shared for casting, the relay doesn't allow it or an administrator has turned casting off, the app tells you why. From iPhone to Apple TV Open Frameleaf on your iPhone and on the Frameleaf TV app, on the same network and signed in to the same Frameleaf account. On a collection page, choose Play on Apple TV, then pick the TV. This uses the Frameleaf TV app rather than a Google Cast receiver. See Apple TV for what you need.

articles.title: Documents and text in photos
articles.description: Find receipts, letters and screenshots by the text in them, copy that text, correct misread lines and review suggested details.
articles.intro: Never hunt for that receipt again. Frameleaf reads the text in your photos: receipts, signs, letters, screenshots, anything with words in it. Search by that text, copy it straight out of the photo, and correct any line that was misread.

headings.title: The Documents view
headings.text: Documents, under Explore in the sidebar, gathers every photo that has text in it. Use its search box to find photos by that text, or by your own corrections to it.

headings.title: Text in this photo
headings.text: Open a photo and its Info panel ends with Text in this photo, below the map. It shows:

headings.title: Suggested details
headings.text: Pull the key details out of receipts and documents in a click. When your administrator turns on Suggest receipt details (in Settings → Search & intelligence → Text, documents & receipts, off by default), the panel suggests details read from the photo's text:

headings.title: Changes on two devices
headings.text: Your edits are safe across devices. Every change is checked against the version of the text you were looking at. If the photo was read again, or you changed the same line on another device in the meantime, the panel reloads with the latest text instead of overwriting it. Just make your change again.

headings.title: Preservation
headings.text: Your corrections travel with your photos in a preservation package, and are restored wherever your library doesn't already have corrections of its own.

articles.text: Never hunt for that receipt again. Frameleaf reads the text in your photos: receipts, signs, letters, screenshots, anything with words in it. Search by that text, copy it straight out of the photo, and correct any line that was misread. The Documents view Documents, under Explore in the sidebar, gathers every photo that has text in it. Use its search box to find photos by that text, or by your own corrections to it. Text in photos is also part of the main search. Text in this photo Open a photo and its Info panel ends with Text in this photo, below the map. It shows: the text as it reads now Show text regions, which draws where each line is on the photo Select text and Copy text Review a photo's text If the photo is yours, you can also review its text: Read text again uses the text recognition destination your administrator chose. If text recognition is off or has no destination, Frameleaf tells you and keeps the photo where it is. People you share the photo with see the text with your corrections applied and without the lines you dismissed. Only you see your review itself. When the photo changes Read again. Your corrections follow the line that now covers the same place in the photo. If the new reading differs from the text you corrected, the line says so. A correction whose text has gone entirely is kept as your own text. Cropped. Text that a crop removes is no longer read, listed or searchable, and your corrections to it are hidden while the crop hides it. Search on a cropped photo only matches its visible text and values you typed yourself. Remove the crop and it all comes back. Locked. A Locked photo's text is part of the photo. It's listed and readable only while your session is unlocked, and locking again clears it from the list and from an open Info panel. Suggested details Pull the key details out of receipts and documents in a click. When your administrator turns on Suggest receipt details (in Settings → Search & intelligence → Text, documents & receipts, off by default), the panel suggests details read from the photo's text: a date a total a reference an email address a phone number Each suggestion shows what the text says, where it was read and how confident the recognition was. You have the final word: a clearly read "12.50" can still be the wrong total, and Frameleaf leaves the order of day and month in a date for you to confirm. For each suggestion you can: Confirm it, or pick one of the Other readings Correct it to your own value Dismiss it Reset your decision so the suggestion shows again Changes on two devices Your edits are safe across devices. Every change is checked against the version of the text you were looking at. If the photo was read again, or you changed the same line on another device in the meantime, the panel reloads with the latest text instead of overwriting it. Just make your change again. Preservation Your corrections travel with your photos in a preservation package, and are restored wherever your library doesn't already have corrections of its own.

articles.title: Duplicates
articles.description: Find photos and videos that look the same, keep the best copy, and merge their details.
articles.intro: Reclaim space and clear the clutter. Frameleaf finds photos and videos that look the same, even when they're different files, groups them, and suggests the best copy to keep. Duplicate detection runs with machine learning on your server and is on by default.

headings.title: How duplicates are found
headings.text: Photos are compared by what they look like, so a resized or re-saved copy is still found. Videos are compared on several frames from inside the video, not just the first one. That finds copies of the same video at different resolutions, and keeps videos that only start the same way, with black frames, title cards or intro screens, apart. By default four frames are compared and two must match.

headings.title: Review duplicates
headings.text: Open Library Care at the bottom of the sidebar, or Settings, then Utilities, and choose Duplicate review. Items appear here as soon as they've been processed and placed in a duplicate group.

headings.title: Whose photos are in a group
headings.text: Duplicate groups only ever contain your own photos, and only you decide what to keep. If some photos in a group are Locked, unlock to review the whole group.

headings.title: What happens to albums, favourites and tags
headings.text: Keep one copy and you lose nothing. When you keep exactly one item and trash at least one other, the details from the trashed copies are merged into the one you keep:

headings.title: Duplicates with partners
headings.text: A partner's copies are skipped when your library already holds the same file, so partner sharing doesn't give you doubles. Duplicates are still detected separately for each person. See Sharing.

headings.title: Saving disk space in a family library
headings.text: Frameleaf also saves disk space with physical deduplication. When several people on the server upload the exact same file, Frameleaf stores it on disk once while each person keeps their own copy in their library, with their own albums, favourites, descriptions, faces, Locked state and permissions. It's purely a storage saving: every account stays private, and no partner sharing is needed.

articles.text: Reclaim space and clear the clutter. Frameleaf finds photos and videos that look the same, even when they're different files, groups them, and suggests the best copy to keep. Duplicate detection runs with machine learning on your server and is on by default. Exact copies are handled for you automatically: an identical file is never stored twice in your library, whether it came from the web app, a phone or the command-line tool. This works even when your administrator turns duplicate detection off. How duplicates are found Photos are compared by what they look like, so a resized or re-saved copy is still found. Videos are compared on several frames from inside the video, not just the first one. That finds copies of the same video at different resolutions, and keeps videos that only start the same way, with black frames, title cards or intro screens, apart. By default four frames are compared and two must match. Administrators can change how similar items must be in the duplicate detection settings, from 0.001 to 0.1. Higher values find more duplicates, and more false matches. Review duplicates Open Library Care at the bottom of the sidebar, or Settings, then Utilities, and choose Duplicate review. Items appear here as soon as they've been processed and placed in a duplicate group. For each group: Click a photo to zoom into both copies at the same point, and move to pan both. Videos can be played side by side from the start. The suggested copy is marked Suggested keeper. Each copy shows its size in pixels and on disk, tags that say how it compares, such as Original format, Highest resolution, Largest file, Most metadata, Lower resolution or Compressed copy, and up to six details where the copies differ, such as the date or camera. Choose which copies to keep. The rest move to the trash. If you keep more than one, you can stack the kept items together instead. Keep all copies keeps every copy. You're always in control: nothing is removed until you choose an action. Suggested keepers When you look at suggestions or choose Keep suggested, Frameleaf preselects what to keep: The native original. A RAW file first, then HEIC or HEIF, over a re-encoded copy such as a JPEG, even when the JPEG is the bigger file. Re-saved and shared copies are often larger but lower quality. The largest file, when every copy is the same kind of file. The copy with the most metadata. Preferring the native original is on by default. Administrators can turn it off with Prefer original format in the duplicate detection settings. You can change any pick before you confirm. Working through many groups Got thousands of groups? Review is built for that: Each decision takes effect straight away and moves you on to the next group. Routine keep and stack decisions don't ask for confirmation. You can undo recent decisions. Select matching groups and Keep suggested decide many groups in one step. A group without one clear suggestion waits for you to choose. Bursts are shown on a contact sheet, so you can pick your favourite frames. Keep several, or stack the burst without deleting anything. Every burst frame is treated as a real original, and stays one when stacked. When the trash is off If your administrator has turned the trash off, the copies you don't keep are deleted permanently. Frameleaf says so in the review and asks you to confirm. Stacking keeps every photo. With the trash on, the space is only freed once the trash is emptied. Whose photos are in a group Duplicate groups only ever contain your own photos, and only you decide what to keep. If some photos in a group are Locked, unlock to review the whole group. How many groups are waiting also shows as Duplicate groups at the top of Missing media and Damaged media in Library Care. articles.title: Editing
articles.description: Non-destructive photo and video editing on the web and in the apps, saved versions, looks and presets, and how edited files are stored.
articles.intro: Edit freely, knowing your original is always safe. Frameleaf saves every edit as a new version and never changes your original file, so you can go back at any time. Downloads give you the edited version by default, with the original one option away.

headings.title: Open the editor
headings.text: Open a photo or video and choose Edit in the viewer. Or select some photos and choose Quick edit in the selection bar.

headings.title: Photo tools
headings.text: The web editor has four tools down its side:

headings.title: Versions
headings.text: Every saved edit is kept as a version, with its edit recipe and its finished file.

headings.title: Edit in another app
headings.text: You can develop a photo, such as a RAW file, in an app like darktable or Lightroom and bring the result back as a new version:

headings.title: Video tools
headings.text: Open a video and choose Edit. The video editor opens on Trim.

headings.title: How edits are stored
headings.text: The original is never written to. Every render reads from it. The edited master is always made fresh from the original and your edit recipe, so editing again never builds up quality loss. It's the best-quality version of your edit, and it's what downloads and exports give you. Download original gets the untouched file. Previews, thumbnails and streaming versions are smaller copies made from the master. They can be ma

headings.title: Restore and upscale
headings.text: Bring old and damaged photos and videos back to life. Restoration makes a separate, improved version and keeps the original as it is. You see a 5-second preview first. It runs on a GPU computer at home, or on Cloud GPU if you choose it. Pick a restoration worker that supports the task and model you want.

headings.title: Studio
headings.text: Turn your library into a film. Studio, in the web app and on iPad and Android tablets, is a multitrack video editor: build a film from your library, grade it, add titles, music and captions, and export on your device or a server worker. See Studio.

articles.text: Edit freely, knowing your original is always safe. Frameleaf saves every edit as a new version and never changes your original file, so you can go back at any time. Downloads give you the edited version by default, with the original one option away. Open the editor Open a photo or video and choose Edit in the viewer. Or select some photos and choose Quick edit in the selection bar. Leave the editor and come back, and your unsaved edits are waiting for you. If the item changed in the meantime, the editor tells you and starts fresh. Photo tools The web editor has four tools down its side: Masks opens from Adjust. Add a radial or linear mask to apply light and colour changes to part of the photo, or outside it when inverted, with feather and amount. Versions lists every saved version of the photo; see Versions. A few helpers make editing quicker: Hold to show the original, or press \ or Y, to compare. Split view shows before and after side by side with a divider you can drag. Double-click a slider to reset it, or reset a whole group. Copy adjustments and Paste adjustments to carry your edit to other photos. A histogram shows the current preview, and warns when highlights or shadows are clipping. Social formats set the crop for a Feed, Portrait 4:5, Landscape, Vertical, Shorts 9:16 or Wide 16:9 post. Fine-tune the framing in Crop. When you're done, choose Save version. Your edit is saved as a new version and rendered from the original; the original is kept. The iPhone and iPad and Android apps have their own editors, with Adjust, Looks, Crop, Clean Up and Masks. Edits made on any device are saved the same way, so they're shared between them. Native app tools The iPhone and iPad and Android apps add perspective correction, Subject and Sky masks, and Remove and restoration tools. On iPhone and iPad, white-balance Auto and the Eyedropper use the photo on the device. Draw with Apple Pencil on iPad or a pen on Android tablets. A tool that needs a server renderer or restoration worker tells you before it starts. Presets A preset keeps your light, colour, effects, detail, look and masks. Applying one never changes the crop. Save as preset from your current settings, and give it a name. Replace a preset with your current settings, or delete it. Versions you already saved with it keep their settings. Presets you make on one device are available on the others. A setting one device has no control for, such as Brilliance from the phone apps, still goes into the photo when you apply the preset there. Versions Every saved edit is kept as a version, with its edit recipe and its finished file. Versions, at the top of the editor, lists Original and each saved version, with the one your library shows marked Current. Choose one to load its settings. All versions opens the full list, where each version offers: Edit from this version loads its settings so you can carry on from there. Show this version makes it the one your library shows. Choose it on Original to go back to the original. Nothing is deleted. Compare with original shows the two side by side. Download as JPEG saves the finished file. Each version shows whether it's Ready, Finishing with its progress, Waiting or Couldn't finish. Rendering happens on your server after you save. You can follow it in Activity, where a Photo version goes from Rendering to Done. If a render fails, it's retried automatically. Edits saved by a newer app are kept safely as they are. You see a note that showing the edit needs a newer version of Frameleaf, and the preview updates once your server is updated. Edit in another app You can develop a photo, such as a RAW file, in an app like darktable or Lightroom and bring the result back as a new version: In the editor, open Edit in another app and choose Export original. Develop it in your other app. Choose Bring back as a version and pick the finished file: JPEG, TIFF, PNG, WebP or HEIF. You can note which app you used. Frameleaf checks that the original hasn't chang

articles.title: Library and timeline
articles.description: Browse your library in three layouts, select and change many photos at once, and find your way around the viewer, folders and supported formats.
articles.intro: All your photos and videos live in one library, and Frameleaf gives you fast ways to browse it, pick out what you want and act on many photos at once. The Library entry at the top of the sidebar opens it, and the rest of the sidebar takes you to Explore (People, Pets, Memories, Places, Map, Tags, Folders and Documents), Albums, Shared spaces and Tools. Library Care sits at the bottom of the sidebar. On a phone-sized

headings.title: Three layouts
headings.text: The library has three layouts. Your filters, sort order, selection and scroll position carry over when you switch between them.

headings.title: Select and change many at once
headings.text: Click a photo's check mark to select it. Shift-click selects everything in between, and clicking a day header selects that day. Nothing is selected when the page opens. The selection bar offers Compare, Quick edit and Open in Studio, plus favourite, add to album, share link, download, stack, change date, description or location, archive, mark sensitive, tag and delete. Deleting can be undone. Select all matching sele

headings.title: The viewer
headings.text: Open a photo to see it on a black background. Tap or click to hide the controls, and swipe down to close.

headings.title: Folders
headings.text: Folders shows your originals the way they're stored on disk, with a folder tree on one side and the photos and videos in the selected folder on the other. A path above the photos lets you click your way back up.

headings.title: Photos from external libraries
headings.text: Your administrator can add folders that already exist on the server, such as a NAS share of old photos, as an external library that belongs to your account. Its photos and videos appear in your timeline and behave like any others: you can open them on the map, add them to albums, favourite and tag them.

headings.title: Uploads, downloads and the trash
headings.text: Upload files or a folder from the top bar, or drag them onto the page. Download gives you an item's current, edited version, and Download original the untouched file. See Uploads and downloads. Deleted items wait in the trash for 30 days by default, and Large files helps you find what takes the most space. See Trash and large files.

headings.title: Supported formats
headings.text: Live Photos and Android motion photos are kept as one item that plays its motion clip.

headings.title: Your originals are never changed
headings.text: Frameleaf never changes your original files. Edits are saved as new versions (see Editing), and descriptions, ratings, dates, locations and tags you change are written to an .xmp sidecar file next to the original (see XMP sidecars).

Use the D, M and Y keys, Ctrl or ⌘ with the scroll wheel, or pinch on a trackpad or touch screen. Years and Months appear as cards. The screen stays awake while it plays, and Reduce Motion switches transitions to fades. To turn it off, or to take it out of the sidebar, go to Settings, then Your preferences, then Tools & sidebar, and change Use or Show in sidebar in the Folders row. articles.title: Library Care
articles.description: Find missing and damaged originals, put back exact verified copies, rejoin Live Photos, and keep your library healthy.
articles.intro: Library Care keeps your library healthy. It checks that every original is there and readable, and helps you fix what isn't with exact, verified copies, never "close enough" ones. It also rejoins split Live Photos and gathers your organising, import and automation tools in one place.

headings.title: Other queues
headings.text: At the top of Missing media and Damaged media, after the number of findings and the scan bar, you'll see the other queues waiting for you. Counts respect privacy: another account's Locked items are never counted, and your own only after you unlock.

headings.title: Scan again
headings.text: Scan again checks every item in your library: is the original there, and does it read back intact?

headings.title: Missing media
headings.text: Select findings and choose Locate originals. In Choose candidate originals, pick where to look: your library storage, your external libraries and, for administrators, the recovery locations set up on the server. Choose Search selected locations. The search runs in the background. Review each candidate. It shows where it was found, whether its checksum is an exact match and whether it opens correctly. If a copy was fo

headings.title: Damaged media
headings.text: Suspected damage and unsupported RAW files wait for review until a check confirms a problem. You act on Confirmed damaged findings:

headings.title: Live Photos
headings.text: An Apple Live Photo is two files, a still photo and a short video. When they're uploaded or imported separately, for example from a backup, a desktop sync or another service's export, they can show up as two unrelated items.

headings.title: Who sees what
headings.text: Each person reviews their own findings. Missing media and Damaged media are administrator tools; an administrator can also review one other account, or all accounts.

headings.title: Preservation packages
headings.text: To keep a verifiable copy of your originals and everything your library knows about them, make a preservation package. See Preservation packages.

headings.title: For administrators
headings.text: Recovery locations are folders Library Care may search for copies, such as a backup drive. Set them with FRAMELEAF_RECOVERY_ROOTS, for example Verified backup=/mnt/backup/photos;/mnt/photos/recovered, and mount them read-only if you can. A candidate must still be a regular file inside its location when it's recovered; a link that leads outside it is refused. Hidden Library Care folders. Kept damaged files, and recove

articles.text: Library Care keeps your library healthy. It checks that every original is there and readable, and helps you fix what isn't with exact, verified copies, never "close enough" ones. It also rejoins split Live Photos and gathers your organising, import and automation tools in one place. Open Library Care at the bottom of the sidebar. It opens Settings, then Library care: Every tool is also in Settings, then Utilities, grouped as Organize, Repair, Import, Automate and Connect. File trash holds stored files that no library uses any more, for example after physical deduplication shared them. Nothing there is deleted automatically: Restore puts a file back in the library it was last in, and Delete permanently removes it from the server's disk. The Library care settings page brings health checks and repair tools together. Open a tool to review its findings, then fix what it found. Select the image to enlarge it. Other queues At the top of Missing media and Damaged media, after the number of findings and the scan bar, you'll see the other queues waiting for you. Counts respect privacy: another account's Locked items are never counted, and your own only after you unlock. Scan again Scan again checks every item in your library: is the original there, and does it read back intact? The scan runs in the background, and you can follow it in Activity and the notifications panel. It saves its place after every small batch, so you can pause, resume or cancel it, close the browser or restart the server, and it carries on from where it stopped. A scan that fails is retried once automatically before the failure is reported. The scan bar shows the last scan, a running one, or a failure. Missing media Select findings and choose Locate originals. In Choose candidate originals, pick where to look: your library storage, your external libraries and, for administrators, the recovery locations set up on the server. Choose Search selected locations. The search runs in the background. Review each candidate. It shows where it was found, whether its checksum is an exact match and whether it opens correctly. If a copy was found in more than one place, choose one and Save candidate choices. Choose Relink verified matches to point each item at its verified copy. Matches are found by their content checksum, never by file name, thumbnail or video length, so only a true copy of the original is ever relinked. A resized, re-encoded or edited copy won't match. Where the copy ends up depends on where it was found. A copy in your library storage, or in the item's own external library, is linked where it is. A copy in a recovery location is copied into your library storage first; recovery locations are only ever read. "Missing" doesn't always mean deleted. The storage may have moved, be offline or have the wrong permissions, or the path may have changed. Check those first. Damaged media Suspected damage and unsupported RAW files wait for review until a check confirms a problem. You act on Confirmed damaged findings: Recover from a verified copy puts back a copy whose checksum matches the original exactly and that opens correctly. Search your library storage and recovery locations, choose a copy, confirm that you've reviewed the evidence and select Record verified recovery. The good copy is placed in a hidden Library Care folder in your library storage, and the damaged file is moved beside it, never over anything, so it's kept for recovery but never imported again as a new item. A damaged file that another item still uses stays where it is. Trash confirmed damage moves damaged items to the trash. You type MOVE CORRUPT MEDIA TO TRASH, enter your PIN if you have one, and the evidence must be from the last day. Each item is checked again as it's moved, and one that no longer fails is kept. A RAW file the server can't read is listed separately. It isn't damaged; the server just doesn't support it. Relinks, recoveries and moves to the trash run in the background with the same p

articles.title: Memories
articles.description: Relive past moments as stories, tune what you see, and turn a memory into a private highlight video.
articles.intro: Memories bring your best moments back to you: this day in past years, trips, birthdays, yearly highlights and stories about the people and pets you've named. Each one plays as a full-screen story, and they stay private to you: nothing is ever shared or published automatically.

headings.title: Kinds of memories
headings.text: Birthdays need a date of birth in People. Pet stories need a named pet with at least five confirmed photos in that month.

headings.title: Find your memories
headings.text: Open Memories from the sidebar. The page is split into:

headings.title: Play a memory
headings.text: A memory opens with a title card, then plays each photo with gentle movement, with the place and date along the bottom. If your device asks for reduced motion, photos fade instead. Progress segments at the top show where you are; click one to jump there. Use the arrow keys to move between photos.

headings.title: Export a memory
headings.text: Export this memory gathers the memory's original photos and videos into a ZIP file on your server. It runs in the background, so you can leave the page; the player shows Exporting 3 of 31 as it goes, and you can cancel it. When it's done, choose Download export. The download stays available for 24 hours.

headings.title: See less of something
headings.text: A memory card's menu lets you see fewer memories like it. Depending on the memory, you can choose:

headings.title: Make a highlight video
headings.text: You can turn a memory into a short highlight video. Choose Highlight video, then:

headings.title: Privacy
headings.text: A memory that contains even one Locked item is hidden entirely while your session is locked. Sharing a memory is always something you choose to do.

headings.title: For administrators
headings.text: New memories are made by the Generate memories nightly task, which is on by default in Settings, then Computers & background work, then Overnight schedule. You can also run Generate memories or Clean up old memories by hand from Settings, then Computers & background work, then Background work.

articles.text: Memories bring your best moments back to you: this day in past years, trips, birthdays, yearly highlights and stories about the people and pets you've named. Each one plays as a full-screen story, and they stay private to you: nothing is ever shared or published automatically. Kinds of memories Birthdays need a date of birth in People. Pet stories need a named pet with at least five confirmed photos in that month. How trips are found A trip is a run of photos where no gap is longer than 20 hours, or 6 hours when the place changes, so a same-day flight starts a new trip. It needs at least two different days and at least eight photos. Days are counted in the local time where the photos were taken, so a trip across time zones still reads as the days you lived through. Fewer repeats Photos taken within 20 seconds of each other, such as bursts and Live Photo pairs, count as one moment. Long trips and yearly highlights pick photos evenly across days or months, so one busy day doesn't drown out the rest. A trip keeps up to 60 photos, and a pet story up to 40. Find your memories Open Memories from the sidebar. The page is split into: Today Upcoming: the next 14 days, when Show upcoming is on Earlier: trips and highlights Each memory card has a menu with Play, Favorite, the show less choices for that memory and Hide memory. A trip to a landmark also offers Save as album, which keeps everything you took there on those days as an album. Hover over a card to see a slow preview. Memory settings The gear on the Memories page opens Memory settings: Show upcoming previews memories for the next two weeks. Only favorites shows only the memories you've marked with a heart. Showing less of lists everything you've asked to see less of, so you can bring it back. Play a memory A memory opens with a title card, then plays each photo with gentle movement, with the place and date along the bottom. If your device asks for reduced motion, photos fade instead. Progress segments at the top show where you are; click one to jump there. Use the arrow keys to move between photos. In the player you can: Show all items in the memory and jump to any of them Rename memory; leave the title empty to go back to the generated one Reorder the photos, moving each one earlier or later Remove from memory a photo that doesn't belong; it stays in your library, and the message that appears offers Undo favourite a single photo, or the whole memory turn on the soundtrack, which uses the sound from the memory's own videos. It's off by default, and there's no music library. Export this memory to download its original files (see below) Make a movie in Studio to keep editing it as a video project At the end, choose Play again or Next memory. Each photo stays on screen for five seconds by default. Change it with Memory display duration (seconds) in Settings, then Your preferences. Export a memory Export this memory gathers the memory's original photos and videos into a ZIP file on your server. It runs in the background, so you can leave the page; the player shows Exporting 3 of 31 as it goes, and you can cancel it. When it's done, choose Download export. The download stays available for 24 hours. See less of something A memory card's menu lets you see fewer memories like it. Depending on the memory, you can choose: Show less of a person or pet, such as Show less of Sam Show less from a day, such as Show less from June 12 fewer of that kind of memory, such as Show fewer trips or Show fewer birthdays Matching memories are removed and Frameleaf stops making new ones. Bring any of them back from Memory settings. Hide memory removes one memory. Its photos stay in your library, and hidden memories can be restored from Hidden memories at the bottom of the page. Make a highlight video You can turn a memory into a short highlight video. Choose Highlight video, then: A resolution the chosen computer can't make is greyed out, with the reason. Choose Render. You can leave the page while it wor

articles.title: iPhone and Android apps
articles.description: Connect, back up and browse with Frameleaf for iPhone, iPad and Android.

How backup works Backup is the same idea on both phones. The details of each screen are in the iPhone and Android guides. Choose what to back up. Everything, only camera photos and videos, or albums and folders you pick. You can skip any album or folder, and choose photos, videos or both. Each original is fingerprinted with SHA-256 on the phone and compared with what your server already has, whether it arrived from this phone, another device, the web app or an import. Anything already there is skipped, so nothing is uploaded twice and you save data. Uploads are resumable. An interrupted upload, a crash, a reboot or a change of network picks up where it stopped. The server checks the result. A photo only counts as backed up when the server's fingerprint matches the phone's. Anything that didn't make it is listed under Not on Server, with the reason and Retry. Edited versions, such as edits from Apple Photos or files like IMG_1-edited.jpg from a gallery app, are uploaded and stacked with their original. Mobile data, battery and charging You decide when backup may run. Both apps can keep videos waiting for Wi-Fi while photos use mobile data, never use mobile data at all, or only run while the phone is charging. On iPhone, backup also pauses in Low Power Mode and Low Data Mode by default. On Android, backup always waits while the battery is low. In the background iPhone. iOS decides when apps may work in the background, so the app makes the most of every chance it gets. It runs an overnight backup when iOS allows it, keeps Back Up Now going after you leave the app and, on iOS 26.1 or later, hands remaining photos and videos to iOS's own background upload. The more often you open the app, the more chances it gets. Android. The app catches up every hour, and starts a backup about 30 seconds after you take a photo. Some phones are strict about battery optimisation and stop background work. If backup tells you battery optimisation is in the way, allow the app to run in the background. Photos stored in iCloud If you use Optimize iPhone Storage in iCloud, the app downloads the full originals from iCloud on Wi-Fi and backs them up, and Backup shows how many iCloud originals are waiting. articles.text: Frameleaf finds the faces in your photos and groups them into people, all on your own server. This page shows what happens behind the People page, and how administrators can tune it for cleaner groups. Two steps: detection, then recognition Face detection finds faces. Frameleaf sends each photo's preview image to your machine learning container, which downloads the model the first time it's needed. A detection model draws a box around each face and gives it a score. Each face is then cropped and passed to a recognition model, which turns it into a set of numbers describing what the face looks like. Those numbers are stored in your database and indexed so similar faces can be found quickly. Facial recognition groups faces into people. It runs once detection has finished. For videos, only the thumbnail is checked for faces. How faces are grouped Think of every face as a point on a map, where similar faces sit close together. For each face, Frameleaf looks for other faces within a certain distance, the Maximum recognition distance. If any of those nearby faces already belongs to a person, the face joins the person of the most similar face. If none does, Frameleaf counts how many similar faces there are, including this one. If there are at least Minimum recognized faces (three by default), the face starts a new person. Faces processed later that are close to it join that person. If there aren't enough, no person is created yet. The face waits until all the other faces in the batch have been processed. If one of its matches has gained a person by then, it joins that person. If not, it's treated as an outlier, such as a stranger in the background. A face that has enough similar faces to start a person is called a core point. A face that doesn't can still join a person through a core point, but can't extend a person on its own. This stops loosely related faces from chaining two different people together. Why upload order matters Grouping works on the faces waiting in the queue at the time, and keeps the people it already made. So the more faces in one batch, the better the groups. Recognition waits for detection and thumbnails to finish before it starts, for this reason. If you uploaded in small batches, or the server kept up with your uploads, the groups may not be as good as they could be. Running recognition again for all faces regroups everything at once and gives the best result. To keep up with new photos, Frameleaf only looks for a handful of the closest matches for each face, rather than every face within the distance. A nightly task, Cluster new faces, then finds unassigned faces that now have matches. The result is very close to grouping everything at once. If you haven't put work into naming yet, rerun recognition for all faces for the best starting point. If you have, name or assign a selection of unassigned faces by hand, then run Facial Recognition for Missing. Frameleaf learns from your choices and assigns more faces automatically. Back up your database first. Settings Recognition settings are in Settings, then Search & intelligence, then Faces & identity, then Advanced: face model and numbers. Small changes work best. If you make one setting stricter, relax another a little to balance it, and the other way round. Face model The models are antelopev2, buffalo_l, buffalo_m and buffalo_s, largest first. Larger models are slower and use more memory but give better results. The default is usually the best choice; pick a smaller one if your server struggles. After changing the model, run Face detection for all photos. Face clarity needed Setting this low finds more faces, but also things that aren't faces, which are hard to clean up and spoil the groups. Every file is checksummed when it's written and can be checked again at any time, so years later you can prove the copy is intact. Restore a package into your library, on this server or another one. Find it in Settings, then Import & protection, then Originals & preservation. A package doesn't include accounts, sharing, shared spaces, server settings, pets, memories or Studio projects (Studio projects travel as project bundles). Keep your server backups and a separate copy of your originals as well. Copies a partner shared with you are your own items, so they're included. Make a package Choose Preview preservation manifest. Include. Under What to preserve, choose Whole library, Favorites, Dates (a range of dates the photos were taken), Albums, or Search, which takes the same words and filters you use in Search, such as person: or year:. To preserve a hand-picked set, such as smart search results, select the items and choose Export for preservation… from the selection bar. Include metadata and edit recipes adds the metadata files, albums, people, tags and edit recipes. Include checksums and a manifest is always on. Include Locked items is only available while your session is unlocked. Verify. The server counts and measures your selection and checks that it fits in one package, up to 100,000 items, and in the free space where packages are written. Nothing is written yet. Manifest. See what the package will hold and, category by category, what a restore brings back. Choose Start export. The export runs in the background and is listed in Activity and in the package list. Closing the page doesn't stop it. You can pause, resume or cancel it, and a paused export carries on from the next item. Each original is copied into the package and checked against the checksum your library recorded for it. Nothing is moved or linked, and your library's files are never changed. An item that fails is tried once more automatically. Anything still failing is listed in the item report, where Retry failed items tries again. A package whose items didn't all copy is marked Incomplete. If an item becomes Locked after you started an export without Locked items, it's skipped. Verify a package Verify files reads the package back: the manifest first, then every original and metadata file against its SHA-256 checksum. The package then shows when it was checked and a count such as 12 match · 0 missing · 0 changed · 0 unexpected, where unexpected files are ones the manifest doesn't account for. A package this server wrote is also compared with the record the server kept when writing it, so a rewritten manifest is reported as changed rather than believed. A package is Not verified until a verification passes. Verify the copy you keep elsewhere too, by uploading it, or, if you're an administrator, by pointing the server at it. Then you know the copy you're relying on is intact, not just the one on the server. articles.text: Locked keeps sensitive photos and videos off your screen without moving them anywhere. A locked item stays in its albums, stacks, favourites and tags, and stays hidden everywhere until you unlock your session with your PIN. It's perfect for anything you'd rather not have on screen during normal browsing: medical photos, prescriptions, card or bank images, identity documents, private family photos and personal records. Locking is just a label. Your albums, stacks, favourites, tags, faces and timeline stay exactly as they are, and unlocking puts everything back where it was. Locked keeps private photos out of sight in Frameleaf. Pair it with full-disk encryption, strong passwords and careful control of who can reach your server, and keep regular backups. If you use automatic detection, review its results. Set up your PIN Locked uses a six-digit PIN. Create it in Settings → Access & security → Locked folder PIN. You can change or clear it there too. Forgotten your PIN? Choose Forgot your PIN? and enter your account password to clear it. Your locked items stay locked. If password sign-in is turned off on your server, your administrator can clear it for you. Lock a photo Lock a photo whichever way suits you: Select photos and choose Mark Sensitive in the selection bar, or open a photo and choose Mark Sensitive under More actions. Mark it sensitive while reviewing it in the Info panel. Upload straight into Locked. In the mobile apps, select photos you own and mark them as NSFW. Locking is instant and needs no PIN, because it only hides things. Unlocking an item asks for your PIN. Stacks and Live Photos lock as a whole. Locking one photo in a stack locks the whole stack, and the video part of a Live Photo locks with its photo. Why an item is locked Every locked item has exactly one lock, which records why: Unlock your session Select Locked in the top bar, near Upload, and enter your PIN. Locked: sensitive content is hidden. Revealed: this session can see it, and the arrow beside it opens the Locked view. Select Revealed to lock again. That hides it straight away and refreshes what's on screen. Unlocking applies to the current session only, so signing out, or using another browser or app, asks for your PIN again. Content hides when you leave this tab, and shows again when you come back, as long as you're still unlocked. Unlocking lasts an hour. Using Frameleaf in the last few minutes of that hour extends it by another hour, so your session locks itself after about an hour without activity. Who sees a locked item Your own devices sync locked items marked as locked, so they stay hidden there too. A bulk change you start while locked skips any item that was locked after you started it. Revealed for this session Once you unlock, every locked item, and everything your Locked rules hide, works like any other item, everywhere, for you: Search finds them, including smart search, text in photos and Ask, and includes them in counts and suggestions. Library views show and count them: the timeline, archive, Explore, memories, people and pets, Best Photos, duplicates, albums, the map, tags and folders. Actions work on them: favourite, archive, add to album, change date or location, delete and download. Studio can place them in a project, use one as a project's poster and export them. They're still yours alone. Sharing isn't offered for a revealed item, and it never becomes an album cover, a featured photo or a profile picture, because those are shown to everyone. When you lock again, they keep every album, stack, tag, person, memory and Studio project they belong to, and disappear from view as before. articles.intro: Type what you remember. Frameleaf's smart search understands the content of photos and videos, so "dog on the beach" or "sunrise over a lake" finds them without any tags. Narrow any search with filters, type filters straight into the search box, or ask a question in everyday words.

headings.text: The results page shows your filters as chips across the top. Click a chip's cross to remove it, or Clear all. From the toolbar you can sort, switch between grid and list, start a slideshow, and see results on a map.

Smart search processes images and search text on the machine learning worker your administrator configured, which normally runs alongside Frameleaf. Press Ctrl K (⌘ K on a Mac) from anywhere. Press / when you're not typing in a field. The search panel opens over the page. As you type, it shows suggestions, matching people, places and pages, and a live count of matches. Start with a word you remember, then refine the matches without leaving the search panel. Select the image to enlarge it. Start with > to switch to the command palette and jump to a page, a setting, a person or a place instead of searching. Search modes The mode menu at the left of the search box chooses what your words are matched against: The text modes match anywhere in the field, and ignore capitals and accents, so cafe finds Café. For example, in Full path, searching for Projects, 3D, Printing or 2026 all find a photo stored at /John/Projects/3D_Printing/2026-07-01/IMG_0001.jpg. Text in photos is more forgiving: it matches words that are close to what you typed, which helps when the text recognition misread a letter. Smart search Smart search compares your words with what's actually in each photo and video, using a CLIP model on your machine learning worker. No tags or captions needed: birthday cake with candles, snow in the mountains or red car at night all work. Results are ranked by how well they match. Frameleaf also gives a boost to photos whose description or recognised text contains your words, so a receipt that says "Whole Foods" rises when you search for it, even if it looks like any other receipt. A few tips: Describe what you'd see, not what it means to you: girl blowing out candles rather than Emma's 5th. Add a filter for the part a picture can't show, such as a person, a place or a date. See Search syntax. Smart search ranks matches rather than filtering them, so a long list of results gets less relevant towards the end. Find similar photos Open a photo and choose Find similar from the viewer's menu to search for photos that look like it. The search panel shows the photo as Similar to a photo, and you can add filters on top. Video moments Searches also show Moments in your videos above the results: video frames that match your words by meaning, and moments you've added whose title or transcript contains them. Only your own videos are searched. See Video moments. Ask about your photos Open the Search page with nothing typed to see Ask about your photos. Type a question in everyday words, or pick one of the examples: favorite videos since 2020 photos from last summer receipts from last year screenshots from last month Frameleaf turns the question into search filters, runs it, and shows What Frameleaf searched for so you can see how it read your question and refine it. What Ask understands Everything else in the question goes to smart search. People, pets and places in a question Names after with or of are matched against the people and pets you've named. Separate several names with and, & or commas: photos of Alice and Sam at the lake. An exact name wins, a person before a pet; otherwise Frameleaf picks the closest name. Hidden people never match, and neither do Locked ones until you unlock. If a name doesn't match anyone, the search still runs and Frameleaf tells you the person match is approximate. For places, use a real city name. Phrases such as "my hometown" or "the beach" aren't treated as places: Frameleaf tells you and searches without a location. Receipts, documents and screenshots are found using the text in them and file names, so these questions skip smart search. Ask returns up to 100 matches by default. If Ask is turned off o

Switch models when you want search in more languages or want to make the most of stronger hardware. Smart search runs on your server or on a machine learning computer on your network. This page is for administrators: changing the model means rebuilding the library's search data, and search fills in as that finishes. Choose for your library Think about three things: the languages people search in, the subjects in your photos, and the memory available to the machine learning worker. Larger models use more memory and processing time, and they shine on some queries more than others. Pick a model offered by your installed release and your configured model source. For multilingual search, try a multilingual model with a few typical queries in each language. Compare the results on your own photos before you reindex the whole library. Benchmarks from other machines are a rough guide. Your own server's memory use and indexing speed are what count. Switch to a new model Note your current model, and make sure the worker can download the new one. Open Settings → Search & intelligence → Visual search → Advanced: search model. Set Search model to the model's exact name and save. Open Settings → Computers & background work → Background work and run the Visual search queue for all photos. Check the server and machine learning logs for failed downloads or memory errors. When indexing finishes, try your typical searches again. Each model needs its own index. If you switch back to an earlier model, rebuild the index for that model too. What else changes Suggested tags, curated smart-album queries and video-moment search also use smart-search data, so give their processing time to finish and take a look afterwards. Your originals and the descriptions you wrote stay exactly as they are. Hardware and where it runs Smart search stays on your network. Speed it up with hardware acceleration on a supported GPU, or run it on another computer with remote machine learning. Models come from your configured model source, and Frameleaf reports a missing model as a failure so you always know where your models come from. See Where models come from.

headings.title: Filters you can type
headings.text: Filter names aren't case sensitive, and neither are the values: Person:jamie works the same as person:Jamie. Values are also matched without accents, so place:Montreal finds Montréal.

articles.text: Type filters straight into the search box and get exactly the photos you want, without opening the filter panel. Mix filters with your own words, and put - in front of a filter to exclude it. This finds photos of Jamie, taken in Banff during 2026, ranked by how well they match "lake at sunset". Click the ? button in the search panel to see every filter at any time. Click one to add it to the search box. Filters you can type Filter names aren't case sensitive, and neither are the values: Person:jamie works the same as person:Jamie. Values are also matched without accents, so place:Montreal finds Montréal. Values with spaces Put a value in double quotes when it has a space: Excluding Put - straight in front of a filter to leave out what it matches: You can exclude every filter except rating:, year:, month:, after:, before: and text:. Put - in front of one of these and it stays as ordinary search text. Combining filters Different filters all have to match: finds videos of Jamie from 2025. Repeating a filter works like this: For "any of these people" instead of "all of them", use the People section of the filter panel and choose Any of. How each filter works person: Matches the names you've given in People, so name someone to search for them. If no one has that name, the filter stays as ordinary search text, so you can see it and fix it. place: Matches the city worked out from each photo's location. See Places. For a country or a state, use the Places section of the filter panel. tag: Matches one of your tags by name. If you have no tag with that name, the filter stays as search text. type: Accepts photo, photos, image, images, video or videos. camera: and lens: camera: first looks for a camera brand in your library with exactly that name, such as camera:Canon. If there isn't one, it looks for camera models containing your words, such as camera:R5, and then for brands containing them. lens: matches any lens name containing your words, such as lens:50mm. Excluding a camera keeps photos with no camera information at all. rating: Takes a number from 0 to 5 and finds that rating or higher. rating:4 finds four- and five-star photos. For an exact rating, rejected or unrated photos, use the filter panel. is: Accepts fav, favorite, favorites, favourite or favourites. Dates So after:2026-08-12 before:2026-08-15 finds photos from 13 and 14 August 2026. Dates use the local time where the photo was taken, the same date you see in the timeline. An impossible date, such as 2026-02-30, stays as search text. file:, path: and text: file: and path: find the words anywhere in the file name or folder path, ignoring capitals and accents. -file: and -path: leave out names that contain the words. text: searches the words Frameleaf read from inside your photos, such as signs, receipts and screenshots. It matches words that are close to what you typed, so a small misreading still matches. Phrases and excluded words The syntax help also lists two forms for your own words: Chips and suggestions As you type, the search panel suggests people, places, tags, cameras, years, media types and filters that match the word you're typing, with their counts. Press Tab or click a suggestion to complete it. When you finish a filter and type a space, it turns into a chip, such as Not Jamie, Camera: Sony or 4★ or more. Click a chip's cross to remove it. A filter Frameleaf can't match stays as text, so you can see it and fix it. Search text can be up to 500 characters. Anything longer is cut, and the panel tells you. Filters that have become chips don't count towards the limit. Examples

articles.text: Everyone on your server has their own private library. Sharing brings them together: give a partner their own copy of your library, build albums with family, or send a link to anyone, and always know exactly who sees what. Partners Share your whole library with a partner on your server. They get their own copy of your photos and videos, in their own library. Open Settings → People & sharing. In Partners & recipient groups, select Add a partner. Choose their account and read what they'll receive. Select Share my library with and their name. They're listed with You share your library with and their name. Partner sharing is one-way. To get your partner's photos, they need to share with you too. The first copy runs in the background. The partner's card shows its progress, such as Copying 120 of 4,000 items, then Up to date when it's done. New photos and albums are copied as you add them. What a partner receives The copies are theirs Each copy is an ordinary item in your partner's library and timeline. It's labelled with where it came from, such as From Sam's library. They can add it to albums, favourite it, edit it or delete it, like any of their own photos. Copies follow your edits. Change a description, location, date, rating, tags, people, or whether it's archived or Locked, and their copy changes too. Album copies follow your album's title, description, cover and photos. Their changes win. Once your partner changes a detail on their copy, that detail is theirs and stops following yours. The other details still follow. Deleting is separate. If you delete a photo, their copy stays. If they delete a copy, it isn't sent again. No doubles. If their library already holds the same file, no second copy is made. It's passed on. What a partner receives also goes to anyone they share their library with. It's never copied back to you. Locked items Your Locked items are copied too. Each copy arrives already locked in your partner's library, and only their own PIN opens it, like their own Locked items. Your PIN is never shared. Items hidden by your Locked rules arrive locked too. Your rules don't become theirs. While their copy follows yours, locking or unlocking it later carries over. Once they change whether their copy is locked, it's up to them. If your partner has no PIN yet, their locked copies stay hidden and they see A partner shared Locked items with you. They can select Set a PIN, or Not now. Storage A copy points at the same stored file as yours, so the server keeps the file once. Each copy still counts in full towards its owner's storage limit. Stop sharing Select Stop sharing next to the partner, then Stop sharing again to confirm. New photos and edits stop reaching them straight away. They keep everything already copied into their library. Those copies stop following your edits. If the first copy was still running, the card shows how many items were already copied. Likes and comments Shared albums come alive with likes and comments. Members can react to the album and the photos in it in the Likes & comments panel. The owner can turn this off under Options → Likes and comments. Leave an album Members can choose Leave on an album shared with them. articles.intro: Built-in smart albums sort your library for you. Frameleaf creates six albums for every user and fills them automatically, so your trips, receipts, screenshots, meals, pets and nature shots are always one click away:

headings.title: Take a photo out
headings.text: If a photo lands in the wrong album, such as a pet on the beach showing up in Travel, remove it from that album as you would from any other. Frameleaf remembers your choice and keeps it out for good, even when the albums are re-evaluated. Its other albums stay as they are.

headings.title: How photos are chosen
headings.text: Each album has two ways to match a photo, and either is enough:

headings.title: For administrators
headings.text: Smart albums are off by default. Turn them on in Settings → Search & intelligence → Categories & smart albums, with Build smart albums. The six albums are created for every active user the first time you turn this on.

headings.title: Troubleshooting

articles.text: Built-in smart albums sort your library for you. Frameleaf creates six albums for every user and fills them automatically, so your trips, receipts, screenshots, meals, pets and nature shots are always one click away: Travel Documents & Receipts Screenshots Food Pets Nature They fill up as AI descriptions finish, based on the tags each photo gets and on what smart search sees in it. In every other way they're ordinary albums: open, share and download them as you like. Your administrator turns them on; see For administrators. You can also make your own smart albums from any search, or with New, then Smart album. Those follow a rule you build yourself; see Albums. Take a photo out If a photo lands in the wrong album, such as a pet on the beach showing up in Travel, remove it from that album as you would from any other. Frameleaf remembers your choice and keeps it out for good, even when the albums are re-evaluated. Its other albums stay as they are. How photos are chosen Each album has two ways to match a photo, and either is enough: Tag triggers. The photo has one of the album's trigger tags from its AI description. CLIP queries. The photo looks enough like one of the album's phrases to smart search. How close it has to be is the album's threshold. Smart albums look at your own photos and add only photos you can already see. Default triggers and queries Every album starts with a CLIP threshold of 0.28. For administrators Smart albums are off by default. Turn them on in Settings → Search & intelligence → Categories & smart albums, with Build smart albums. The six albums are created for every active user the first time you turn this on. For the best results, turn on smart albums once descriptions are working. Description tags feed the tag triggers, and CLIP queries use smart-search data from a reachable worker. See the setup order. Settings for each album Each album has its own section: Update albums now, at the bottom of the page, runs every album. It shows how many described photos will be checked before you confirm. Photos are added to or removed from albums as needed, and photos people took out stay out. Tag triggers Tag matching ignores capitals, and treats hyphens and spaces the same, so golden-retriever and golden retriever both work. Make your albums richer with additions like these: Threshold The threshold applies to CLIP queries; a tag trigger matches whenever the tag is there. Start with 0.28. Lower it to 0.25 if an album looks sparse, or raise it to 0.32 if it's noisy. The useful range is 0.2 to 0.4. CLIP queries Each phrase is compared with each photo's smart search data. A photo joins the album when its similarity to any of the phrases reaches the album's threshold. CLIP queries work alongside tag triggers, and Frameleaf records which one matched. CLIP queries use smart search and the machine learning server. If the server can't be reached, tag triggers keep working, CLIP matching is skipped, and the server log shows a warning. Phrases are encoded once per model and reused, so re-evaluating is quick, and they're encoded again automatically when you change the smart search model. Custom categories The same settings page has two options for the smart albums people build from a search: Rules add information and always respect people's own decisions. Updating albums Update this album works on that album alone, so use it after changing one album's triggers. You can update different albums at the same time, and if one is already running, Frameleaf tells you instead of running it twice. Re-evaluating uses the description tags and search data you already have, so it's fast. If that data is missing, run the relevant processing jobs first. Troubleshooting A photo never appears in an album Check, in order: Smart albums are on, and so is that album. The photo's description has finished. articles.title: Tags
articles.description: Organise photos with your own nested tags, bring in tags from other apps, and use the tags Frameleaf suggests.
articles.intro: Tags let you label photos and videos your own way, then find them again in a click. Nest tags inside other tags to build a tree that suits your library, such as Hobbies/Hiking or Family/Holidays/Christmas.

headings.title: Turn on tags
headings.text: Open Settings → Your preferences → Tools & sidebar. In the Tags row, turn on Use. To keep a Tags link in the sidebar, also turn on Show in sidebar.

headings.title: Add a tag
headings.text: Open a photo or video and show its info panel. In the tags area, choose to add a tag. Pick an existing tag, or type a new one to create it.

headings.title: Browse by tag
headings.text: Open Tags from the sidebar, or click a tag in a photo's info panel. The Tags view shows your tags as a tree, with the photos and videos for the tag you choose.

headings.title: Search by tag
headings.text: Type tag: and the tag's name in the search box: tag:water. Put - in front to leave a tag out: -tag:screenshot. Two tag: filters find photos with both tags. See Search syntax. In the filter panel, the Tags section picks one or more tags. Under Library status, Untagged finds photos with no tags, and Has tags can be set to Yes or No.

headings.title: Import tags from an existing library
headings.text: Bring your existing tags with you. If your photos already had tags when you uploaded them, an administrator can rerun the metadata extraction job for all photos to read them in.

headings.title: Suggested tags
headings.text: Frameleaf tags photos for you with what smart search sees in them, such as beach, forest, dog or cake. It compares each photo with a built-in list of about 300 everyday labels covering scenes, objects, animals, food, activities, transport and weather, and adds the closest matches.

headings.title: Tags from AI descriptions

articles.text: An XMP sidecar is a small .xmp file that sits next to a photo or video and stores details about it, such as a description, rating or keywords, without touching the original file. Sidecars let your descriptions, ratings and tags move freely between Frameleaf and your other photo apps, while your originals stay untouched. Frameleaf uses them in both directions: Reading. When Frameleaf reads a photo's details, it also reads the sidecar next to it. Writing. When you change a description, rating or tags, Frameleaf writes the change to the sidecar too, so other apps can see it. Your original is never changed. Lightroom, darktable, digiKam and many other photo apps can be set to write their changes to .xmp files instead of the original. Frameleaf picks those up. Which fields are read and written Frameleaf works with the fields below. When it writes, it merges them into the existing file, so everything else in the sidecar stays just as it was. Everything else, such as the creator, source, other IPTC fields and Lightroom's edits, stays safely in the .xmp file for your other apps, though Frameleaf doesn't search it. Frameleaf writes the sidecar automatically after you edit a description, a rating or tags. Naming A sidecar must share the name of its photo or video: If both IMG_0001.jpg.xmp and IMG_0001.xmp exist, Frameleaf uses IMG_0001.jpg.xmp. Uploads When you upload with the command-line tool, Frameleaf looks for an .xmp file next to each photo: Detect. A sidecar next to the photo is found. Copy. The photo and the sidecar are both copied into your library storage, and the sidecar is renamed to match the photo, for example IMG_0001.jpg and IMG_0001.jpg.xmp. Read. The details in the table above are read from the sidecar. Keep in step. When you later change the description, rating or tags in Frameleaf, the copied sidecar is updated too. External libraries For an external library, the files stay where they are: Detect. Sidecars next to the photos in the folder are linked to them when the library is scanned. Nothing is moved or renamed. Read. The same fields are read from each sidecar. Write back. When Frameleaf can write to the folder, later changes, such as a rating or tags, are written back to the sidecar on disk. Frameleaf can't write sidecars to a folder mounted read-only, and changes to descriptions, ratings and tags on those files may not be saved, with no warning. If you want your edits written back, ask your administrator to make sure the library folder is writable. Re-reading sidecars Edited sidecars in another app? A Frameleaf server you can sign in to. For Frameleaf Cloud services: a server linked to Frameleaf Cloud. You can also use your own remote access connection. The app uses a dark theme. The app looks for Frameleaf servers on your network. It only looks for Frameleaf servers and doesn't read your Wi-Fi name. Enter a server address, then sign in with your email and password, or with Sign in with your organisation if the server uses its own sign-in provider. When a server is found, a card slides up with its name, your role and "Online · on this Wi-Fi". Choose Connect, Not Now or Don't offer again. After you connect, it asks whether to back up this phone to that server. Set up a brand-new server from your phone On your home network you can claim a server that has no administrator yet. There's no setup code. Setup only works on the same Wi-Fi as the server, and only until it has an administrator, so set a new server up soon after installing it. Choose Set up on the server's card. Give the server a name. Link it to your Frameleaf account with Sign in with Frameleaf. You become the owner without a separate server password. On a server with Frameleaf Cloud, the app always uses Sign in with Frameleaf and doesn't offer a password. If you'd rather use a password administrator there, for example without a Frameleaf account, create it on the server's first-run web page instead. On a server without Frameleaf Cloud, the app creates the first administrator with your email, name and password. That account works on its own, and you can reach it over a VPN or your own HTTPS server address. Optional Cloud services each have their own short setup, which you can do whenever you like. A server that's already linked A server on your Wi-Fi that's already linked to a Frameleaf account is never set up or linked again. It appears as a Join card with a Sign in with Frameleaf button, or as Connect if it's already in your account. If the server has no administrator yet, the first sign-in of the account that owns it creates the administrator. Several servers Every server is listed with your role and its route: Home (your network), Direct or Relay (the Frameleaf relay, part of remote access). The app tries every route at once and prefers Home. You'll see lines like "Connected at home · 3 ms" or "Offline · can't reach it from here". Over the relay, previews always load, but full originals and videos wait for a faster route unless you allow them in Settings, then Privacy and lock. Both are off by default. Remove a server to delete this phone's copy of its library, caches and queue. Nothing is deleted from the server. Servers behind a proxy Most people never need this. A server at home, Frameleaf Cloud remote access and the Frameleaf relay all connect without it.
